about: The public costume-vocabulary catalog: the one list of lazy-shortcut phrases. scripts/scan_output.py scans with it; the v5 Stop hook keeps a short built-in subset (synthesis/reply_check.py) that tests/test_shortcut_catalog.py holds to this file. Each entry's rationale and rewrite are explained in references/costume-vocabulary.md.

categories.backward_compat: Preserving old APIs / paths / behaviors when the user has stated breaking changes are fine.
categories.minimal_diff: Leaving half-applied work as a follow-up. Surfaces as residual styling, residual stale references, half-migrated code.
categories.asking_as_shortcut: Surfacing decisions as questions when the user's stated constraints already determine the answer.
categories.deferral: Pushing real work to 'later' / 'follow-up' / 'next phase' when the user has explicitly said 'complete this, no shortcuts.'
categories.archive_value: Leaving stale content under labels like 'archive' or 'historical reference' when the user wants clean public-facing artifacts.
categories.dismissal: Dismissing user-raised concerns as 'not a real issue' or 'theoretical' instead of solving them.
categories.scope_excuse: Using 'pre-existing' / 'out of scope' / 'not introduced by this change' to avoid fixing problems in code being actively modified.
categories.effort_rationale: Deciding a recommendation by implementation cost when the user has removed cost from the decision set.

phrases.rationale: Cost comparison presented as the deciding pro when the user optimizes for best.

phrases.rationale: Cheapness scored as virtue without the user's constraint set.
phrases.replacement: Only 'cheaper with merits equal' survives; then cheapness is a tiebreak, not the reason.
